summary: Clarify tiered throttling semantics and recommended rate-limit config for mixed realtime + batch workloads
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429s while running a hybrid workload: hundreds of short-lived realtime streaming sessions interleaved with large batch embedding uploads. They are on a Dedicated pool and have configured per-route rate limits, but 429s appear to originate shortly after a stable steady-state throughput is reached.

Impact: Affects production search features for ~50k end-users during peak (Europe hours). Customer sees failed sessions and increased client retry loops resulting in UX errors. No data loss reported; failures are throttling-related.

Environment: dedicated pool (eu-west), API gateway in front, dedicated token-level quotas configured in Console via per-route rules. Customer uses ephemeral session keys for streaming and longer-lived API keys for batch.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start 200 parallel streaming connections with ephemeral keys (avg session length 3s, messages every 200ms).
2) Kick off a background batch embedding job with 8 workers, each uploading 10k items spread over 30 minutes.
3) Observe 429s reported by the client around minute 6-10 of the run.

Observed logs / traces provided: trace IDs [trace-eu-1182, trace-eu-1183, trace-eu-1187]. Example server-side entry shows: "rate_limiter: quota_exceeded token_bucket=tenant:eu-west window_ms=10000 count=5120 limit=5000". Edge logs show multiple connections sharing the same tenant token count key.

Customer asks: 1) Why are ephemeral short-lived streaming sessions causing tenant-level token exhaustion when routes are configured? 2) Best-practice rate-limit and burst settings for mixed realtime + batch on a Dedicated pool. 3) Any Console flags or recommended per-route isolation settings to avoid cross-route exhaustion.

Desired outcome: Clear guidance to eliminate UX-impacting 429s and recommended config to safely run their mix of workloads without over-provisioning GPUs.

investigation_notes: Reviewed rate-limiter implementation: two-level accounting (route-level buckets if route_isolation flag is enabled, otherwise aggregated to tenant bucket).

Edge normalization: ephemeral keys sometimes surface as 'shared' on edge due to host affinity; when route isolation is off, all increments map to tenant token bucket at start-of-session. This explains early spike counts.

Observed default burst_window_ms=10000 and default tenant bucket size configured to 5000 tokens for this customer. Short-lived sessions with frequent messages can cause count to exceed limit before batch traffic is fully throttled.
Confirmed console UI includes an 'apply_on_pool' toggle which must be set for Dedicated pools; customer had created rules but not applied to their pool.
Examined related PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/876 which introduced safe toggles for per-route isolation earlier this year.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Enabled per-route isolation in a test namespace and validated reproduction stopped producing tenant-level 429s. During maintenance window we will: 1) set route_isolation=true for live pool, 2) create separate route tokens for realtime and batch, 3) increase tenant burst_capacity to 7500 temporarily, and 4) enable conservative autoscale headroom for Dedicated pool.

Recommended long-term config changes and best practices provided to customer: 1) Use per-route buckets for realtime routes and set small concurrency windows to contain bursty short sessions. 2) Separate realtime traffic from large batch uploads (different API routes) and tag them in Console for distinct token buckets. 3) For ephemeral keys: prefer short reuse period (reuse keys across multiple short sessions rather than generating high-fanout ephemeral keys) to avoid edge fan-out counting. 4) Configure client-side backoff: exponential with jitter, initial_delay=200ms, max_retries=6, and respect Retry-After header. 5) If sustained high throughput for batch, consider provisioning additional Dedicated capacity or move batch to off-peak windows.

Rollout notes: Priya to coordinate configuration change during next maintenance window (2026-03-15 02:00 UTC). Post-change, monitor rate-limiter metrics and tenant token counts for 24 hours. Follow-up task: create public KB article for 'mixed realtime + batch rate-limiting guidance' and link to Console screenshots.
